monolithOutput.summary: PR #838 tests passed despite missing production path side effects and unreachable high-confidence upgrade logic due to hardcoded unsafe flags and incorrect triage fallbacks.
monolithOutput.rootCause: Design: The diagnostic gate architecture relies on hardcoded safety flags (isUnsafeHighConfidence=false) and lacks dynamic evaluation, causing the test suite to bypass critical production path validations.

violatedPrinciples.title: Dynamic Safety Evaluation
violatedPrinciples.rationale: Safety gates must be evaluated dynamically based on runtime context rather than hardcoded to false, ensuring production-side effects are never silently bypassed.

violatedPrinciples.title: Triage-Production Alignment
violatedPrinciples.rationale: Agent triage logic must not fall back to legacy diagnostic gates when a safe path is identified, preventing test suites from diverging from actual production behavior.

evidence.note: Owner report indicates llm.ts triage incorrectly calls evaluatePainDiagnosticGate post-triage, and gate-block-helper.ts hardcodes isUnsafeHighConfidence=false.
Pain Diagnostic (PD) failed to auto-generate pain/candidate, indicating missing trigger logic for production path side effects.
CLI-submitted pain lacks host trace, but owner reason explicitly cites hardcoded flags and triage fallback as direct causes of test green-light failure.

recommendations.description: Block PRs containing hardcoded unsafe confidence flags or incorrect post-triage gate calls.
recommendations.action: Fail CI check and require dynamic evaluation logic before merge.

recommendations.description: Enforce dynamic safety gate evaluation and production-path mirroring in all diagnostic workflows.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Safety gates must dynamically evaluate runtime context; test suites must explicitly validate production path side effects to prevent silent bypasses.
